subject.title: doctor --fix migrates codex/gpt-5.5 to openai/gpt-5.5, then Codex app-server startup times out on 2026.6.1

question: Should `openclaw doctor --fix` automatically canonicalize legacy Codex model refs to `openai/*` when the Codex app-server route may not be proven healthy, or should it retain/warn for unsafe legacy Codex state?
rationale: This is a shipped doctor migration and provider-routing compatibility choice; code inspection can show the current behavior and candidate fixes, but maintainers must choose the upgrade policy and proof bar.

options.title: Adopt retained-route migration plan
options.body: Rebase and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93180 so doctor only migrates legacy Codex routes when the migration plan proves auth/runtime/session state is safe, and otherwise retains with a warning.

options.title: Treat as startup-only
options.body: Keep the current migration policy and land only the startup-timeout work if maintainers decide the reported failure is solely an app-server initialize boundary.

options.title: Keep automatic canonicalization
options.body: Accept the current doctor rewrite as intentional and document/operator-recover the breakage, but this explicitly owns the risk to existing Codex-backed setups.

recommendation.title: Adopt retained-route migration plan
recommendation.body: Rebase and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93180 so doctor only migrates legacy Codex routes when the migration plan proves auth/runtime/session state is safe, and otherwise retains with a warning.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenAI provider identity and doctor migration history makes this the strongest routing owner for the policy choice.
